chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'What is your view if she gets pregnant?' He said, 'It is his child.'
ai.seo_question: Who is considered the father of a child born from temporary marriage (Mut'ah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that paternity in temporary marriage (*Mut'ah*) is established through conception, mirroring the general principle of *nasab*. This ruling underscores the stability of lineage within the Shia legal framework, ensuring the child’s rights to inheritance and identity are secured regardless of the marriage's duration.
